topic: DeepSeek Harness Trace Compare: Visualizing Agent Exploration

key_points: DeepSeek Harness (dsh) is a developer-preview agent harness, MIT-licensed, source-included on GitHub (deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)

Headline promise: 'Every run is traceable' — everything the model sees is recorded in an append-only session log: system prompts, reasoning, tool calls and results, subagent scheduling, and every context injection
Built on Cordis plugin system — every capability is a plugin: models, tools, skills, sessions, sandboxes, loops, scheduling, UI
~230K stars; topic tags ai-agents, cordis, dsh, dsh-plugin
Ships a session-query package exposing session reads, traces, filters, and search (ctx.sessionQuery)
Tool catalog exposes session_event_trace / session_trace tools for programmatic trace access
Official UI shows explicit trajectory tabs with detailed, per-step agent actions — a core visualization affordance praised by early testers for being explicit about what the agent did
Contrasted in HN discussion with US models that obfuscate chain-of-thought
747-point HN thread on the developer preview — the 'every run is traceable' append-only log is widely called the killer feature
Commenters note the raw trace is hard to reason about, so comparison/visualization tooling is the gap dsh needs
Authors confirm it's an early preview under MIT license; strict tool-call JSON schema validation praised as better than Codex
Commenters ask for harness comparisons (same model + different harnesses) and note trajectory tabs are visually excellent
Community Tauri desktop shell for DeepSeek Harness (by BitFun) — third-party GUI layer on top of the harness
Signals a gap/surge of community tooling around visualizing dsh session data

stats.fact: DeepSeek Harness launched as a developer preview in mid-2026 and quickly reached #1 on Hacker News with ~747 points on its launch thread.
The GitHub repository deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness had climbed to roughly 230K stars (created 2026-08-13), with topics ai-agents, cordis, dsh, dsh-plugin.

The session store is an append-only, event-sourced SessionEvent log — the single source of truth for an agent's entire interaction history; LLM message history is derived from the log, never stored separately, and replay is re-derivation from the same events.

The event vocabulary (SessionEventMap) includes turn/start, turn/end, step/start, step/end, user/message, and system-prompt events, with sequence numbers kept contiguous and every event stored lossless as JSON.

dsh exposes session lineage traces (SessionLineageTrace) with parents in immediate-to-outward order and a forest of nested direct descendants, plus session_query/session_trace tools and OpenTelemetry session-telemetry backend.

DeepSeek Harness is MIT-licensed and built on Cordis, which adds hot-reload and dynamic enable/disable of plugins including UI components — a plugin system authors explicitly tied to agent-harness self-improvement use cases.

angles: The append-only session log is the 'black box recorder' of an agent — what makes dsh fundamentally more inspectable than model providers that obfuscate chain-of-thought.

Traces are the ground truth, but raw traces are hard to reason about; the real value is visualization (trajectory tabs) and comparison (side-by-side of two exploration runs) — the 'compare' in the topic.
How to visualize agent exploration: session lineage trees (parent/child/subagent), step-by-step tool-call timelines, and event-sourced replay from the same log.
Practical guide: how to read a dsh trace, extract session events (session_query / session_trace), and render an exploration map of what the agent tried, failed, and retried.
Compare tooling angle: dsh vs Claude Code / Codex / Pi — first-party harness advantage, and why 'same prompt + different harness' comparisons are the open question in the community.
The community tooling gap: Tauri GUI shells and third-party session viewers emerging because visualization is not yet a first-class product surface.
MIT license + everything-is-a-plugin means trace-format and visualization are extensible — an ecosystem play rather than a closed feature set.
